note: Authored by Lane H against FIELD_CONTRACT.md (EgD-CDK-FIELDS-v2) and ALIGNMENT_BRIEF.md. Reads docs/model/fields.json (Lane G) for live counts where present, and the eve-datasphere-sovereign repo's schema/sap-modules/*/TABLES.yaml + tables/*.yaml for definition status. Static fallback values below are used if the runtime fetch of sap-crosswalk.json is unavailable.

layers.title: Master data
layers.summary: The nouns of the business — the customer, the truck, the person, the vendor, the account. These persist across every transaction and change slowly.

pairings.dealer_label: the customer record — fleet account, walk-in owner, or company
pairings.acdoca_relevance: Feeds ACDOCA's KUNNR (customer) coefficient field on every receivable line; the counterparty identity that lets a journal line answer “who owes this.”
pairings.note: Full API reach, both SAP tables field-defined in the sovereign repo. The cleanest pairing in the twin.

pairings.dealer_label: the truck — VIN or stock number
pairings.acdoca_relevance: Equipment number carries into ACDOCA as a statistical/technical object reference on service and warranty lines, not a posting key itself.
pairings.note: Partial API reach (Fortellis exposes core unit data, not full lifecycle history), but both SAP analogues are field-defined.

pairings.dealer_label: the technician, advisor, or counter person
pairings.acdoca_relevance: Employee/personnel number is the seed for the interaction record's per-human attribution — the column set the doctrine calls Layer 3.
pairings.note: HR module in the sovereign repo is inventory-only — TABLES.yaml lists PA0001/PA0002 but no field-level YAML exists yet. CDK reach itself is also only partial.

pairings.dealer_label: who we buy from — parts suppliers, sublet shops, PACCAR itself
pairings.acdoca_relevance: Feeds ACDOCA's LIFNR (vendor) coefficient field on every payable line — the counterparty side of AP.
pairings.note: Zero API reach at CDK — file/screen export only — even though both SAP tables are already field-defined and waiting on the sovereign side.

pairings.acdoca_relevance: SKA1/SKB1 resolve the RACCT (G/L account) coefficient on every ACDOCA line — without it a journal line has no account to sit in.
pairings.note: No API reach — the chart of accounts comes out by export or screen capture. SAP side is fully defined and ready to receive it.

layers.title: Cost objects
layers.summary: The verbs of the business — the repair order as an internal order, its labour and parts lines, the department it settles to.

pairings.dealer_label: the RO — the job itself, header to close
pairings.acdoca_relevance: AUFK's order number (AUFNR) is the cost-object key that every settled ACDOCA line for the job carries — the thread that ties labour, parts, and sublet back to one repair.
pairings.note: Full CDK API reach on the RO itself, but AUFK — the exact table the RO keys on — is inventoried in three modules (co, pm, pp) and field-defined in none of them. AFIH (service view) is defined. This is the single most important gap to close.

pairings.dealer_label: the hours a tech billed to the job
pairings.acdoca_relevance: AFVC operations confirm into COEP actual-cost line items, which post to ACDOCA as activity-type-valued cost lines against the order.
pairings.note: Full API reach, both SAP tables field-defined. Clean end-to-end pairing.

pairings.dealer_label: the parts issued to the job
pairings.acdoca_relevance: MSEG goods-issue movements value through MBEW and post the material consumption line to ACDOCA against the order's cost object.
pairings.note: Full API reach, MSEG/MKPF both field-defined. Valuation (MBEW) is also defined.

pairings.dealer_label: the department the RO settles to — service, parts, body shop, F&I
pairings.acdoca_relevance: CSKS resolves the KOSTL (cost centre) coefficient that every settled labour and parts line carries on ACDOCA — the department dimension of the whole ledger.
pairings.note: Zero CDK API reach — department/cost-centre structure is a setup table pulled by screen export only — and this is precisely the dimension every settlement line depends on.

pairings.dealer_label: sublet and outside-purchase paperwork on the RO
pairings.acdoca_relevance: EKKO/EKPO drive the goods-receipt/invoice-receipt lines that post sublet cost to the order, then to ACDOCA on settlement.
pairings.note: No CDK API reach, but EKKO/EKPO are fully field-defined on the sovereign side — ready the moment an export path exists.

layers.title: The ledger
layers.summary: Where value lands — the accounting schedule, the journal, and the ACDOCA line with its ESG and interaction columns.

pairings.dealer_label: the open-item schedule behind a GL balance — RO receivables, warranty receivables, stock
pairings.acdoca_relevance: Open-item subledgers behind a reconciliation account are exactly what an accounting schedule is — the assignment field (ZUONR) is the schedule's control key on the ACDOCA line.
pairings.note: Zero API reach at CDK, and the SAP analogues (BSID/BSIK) are inventoried but not field-defined on the sovereign side either. Both halves of this pairing are still open.

pairings.acdoca_relevance: BKPF/BSEG are the classic-ledger shape that ACDOCA unifies in S/4 — every BSEG line has a live ACDOCA twin at posting time.
pairings.note: Partial API reach at CDK (some journal posting visibility via Fortellis), and both classic-ledger SAP tables are field-defined.

pairings.cdk_label: ACDOCA line (destination, not a CDK object)
pairings.dealer_label: the single ledger line the whole repair order eventually becomes

sap_tables.role: Universal journal entry line item — the sovereign spine itself

pairings.acdoca_relevance: This is the spine. Every other row in this table points here.
pairings.note: ACDOCA is fully field-defined in the sovereign repo. The ESG score columns and interaction record columns described in the doctrine are DRAFT v0, not yet ratified or added as columns — see the gap panel.

pairings.dealer_label: the OEM warranty receivable on an RO

sap_tables.role: No native SAP object — closest conceptual analogue is a service notification (QMEL/IW51) tied to a debit-memo receivable

pairings.acdoca_relevance: Settles to its own receivable schedule, which then posts to ACDOCA the same as any other receivable line — but the claim itself has no clean SAP table shape.
pairings.note: No CDK API reach and no clean SAP analogue at all — the honest answer is this is dealer-specific and stays dealer-specific until PACCAR's PRWS schema is mapped.

no_api_reach.label: GL Account Master
no_api_reach.why: Chart of accounts is a setup export, not an API object.

no_api_reach.label: Accounting Schedule
no_api_reach.why: Subledger/open-item view exists only on screen (FBL3N-equivalent report).

no_api_reach.label: Warranty Claim
no_api_reach.why: PACCAR PRWS integration, not a dealer-facing REST endpoint.

no_api_reach.label: Purchase / Receipt Document
no_api_reach.why: AP/receiving documents are file-export or screen only.

sap_tables_inventoried_not_defined.why: The order master the repair order itself keys on — listed in three module inventories, field-level YAML written in none.
Cost totals, internal postings — inventory only.
Cost totals, external postings — inventory only.
Cost elements by controlling area — inventory only.
Open customer items — the accounting-schedule analogue — inventory only.
Employee org-assignment infotype — HR module has an inventory list but zero field-level YAML files exist yet for any HR table.
Employee personal-data infotype — same HR gap.

settle_on_login.item: Whether CDK's GL journal export exposes a stable schedule control key (ZUONR-equivalent) or only a free-text reference field.
The exact cost-centre / department suffix convention across all nine Peterbilt Atlantic rooftops — assumed consistent, not yet seen.
Whether the AP/purchase-receipt export includes a sublet-vs-parts flag needed to route EKKO/EKPO vs. MSEG cleanly.
Whether warranty claims carry a PACCAR PRWS claim number we can use as a durable cross-system key.
Report-catalogue confirmation that a chart-of-accounts export and vendor-master export actually exist as scheduled reports, not just ad hoc screen pulls.

worked_example.title: One repair order, walked end to end

steps.dealer: A truck rolls onto the lot. The service writer opens a repair order against the customer and the unit.
steps.sap: An internal order is created: AUFK header, AFIH service-order extension, keyed by order number (AUFNR).

steps.dealer: A technician clocks hours against labour operations on the RO — diagnosis, repair, road test.
steps.sap: Operations post as AFVC records; time confirmations write actual-cost line items to COEP against the order.

steps.dealer: Parts are picked and issued against the RO from the parts department's shelf stock.
steps.sap: A goods-issue movement writes MSEG (valued through MBEW), with MKPF as the document header — material consumption posts to the same order.

steps.dealer: The RO closes. Labour, parts, and any sublet are totalled and the job invoices to the customer, warranty, or internal account.
steps.sap: The order settles: COEP actual costs roll up and the settlement rule (pay-type driven) allocates the total to the correct receivable and cost-centre destinations.

steps.dealer: The money lands in the dealer's accounting schedule — the open-item list behind the receivable GL account, waiting for cash or warranty reimbursement.
steps.sap: An open item posts behind a reconciliation account — BSID (customer) or BSIK (vendor/warranty payer) — with the order number as the assignment/reference key.

steps.dealer: The journal entry hits the general ledger — department, account, amount, all tied back to this one job.
steps.sap: BKPF header + BSEG line items post the classic-ledger shape of the entry.

steps.dealer: The job is now one line in the dealer's financial picture — department revenue, cost, and absorption for the month.
steps.sap: The same event lands as one or more ACDOCA lines — company code, GL account, cost centre, order reference — plus, once ratified, its ESG score triple (E, S, G) and its interaction record naming which technician, advisor, and counter person contributed, weighted by causal share.
